page: Amazon Web Services c5n.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 10.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 2.62 GB of memory per core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX and AVX-512, alongside AES cryptography and FMA.

This instance does not include local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the c5n.xlarge demonstrates modest processing capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register in the bottom 25%. However, the instance achieves average performance in specific workloads, such as single-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench text processing, and text generation for small 135M parameter language models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5n.xlarge offers a dedicated compute profile with enhanced network capabilities, though its raw processing and memory speeds are lower relative to newer hardware generations. It is best suited for network-bound workloads, basic web serving, lightweight text processing, and utility computing tasks that require dedicated Intel Xeon cores and AVX-512 support without demanding high memory density or local storage.
